week.narrative:
The week's dominant fact was model volume: 24,465 new models were published, and the Qwen family alone accounted for 8,397 of them — more than the 4,484 spread across all other identified open families combined, and far ahead of Llama at 1,189, Gemma at 657 and Mistral at 111. A large block, 9,327 of 24,465, could not be resolved to a family, so the family picture is directional rather than exact; even so, Qwen is clearly the base that builders derived from most. Those models drew 9,237,513 downloads and 10,073 likes, so attention was concentrated in downloads rather than in explicit endorsement.

On the Spaces side, 5,842 were created and every one of them was classified (100.0% coverage), so the category breakdown below can be relied on. Chat and assistants led the named use cases at 903, followed by image generation at 582, data analysis at 461, document AI at 341 and voice and audio at 339; the largest single bucket, however, was everything else at 1,822, meaning most new Spaces did not fall into a recognisable product category at all. Audiences were similarly diffuse, with media and entertainment at 9.7%, consumer at 9.4%, education at 7.3% and scientific research at 7.1% clustered closely, and enterprise productivity (5.7%) and e-commerce (5.2%) trailing.

Tooling remained lightweight: Static led with 3,088 Spaces against Gradio's 2,049, with Docker at 531 and Streamlit at only 108, which points to a lot of demo-grade and non-interactive publishing rather than served applications. Named techniques were thin throughout — vision-language at 7.0%, agentic at 6.5%, diffusion at 5.4%, multimodal at 5.3%, and tool use and RAG both at 3.5% — and Spaces attracted just 739 likes in total, so engagement stayed overwhelmingly on the model side of the hub.
